rationale: Interactive sensemaking and formal artifact issuance have different users, jobs, state, runtimes, economics, failure modes and independently adopted implementations; retaining one product would make its consistency and authority boundary incoherent.

name: Interactive Analytics Exploration
sovereign_question: How can an analyst iteratively inspect, select, compare and navigate semantically bound analytical results while preserving reversible view state and never mutating source or business state?

adoption.finding: Superset, Tableau and Qlik independently expose exploration, chart, sheet and dashboard adoption surfaces.
adoption.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

authority.finding: The product may publish an interactive artifact but does not issue a formal statement, deliver a filing or authorize an operational effect.
authority.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

economics.finding: Interactive BI/exploration is independently deployed, operated, supported and capacity-planned.
economics.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

interface.finding: Declarative visualization specs plus chart/dashboard APIs and exported definitions provide explicit integration and exit surfaces.
interface.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

job.finding: The owned job is reversible sensemaking through views, selections, comparisons, pivots, drills and bookmarks.
job.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

lifecycle.finding: Exploration artifacts move through draft, bound, reviewed, published, superseded and retired while sessions and bookmarks have separate state.
lifecycle.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

market_evidence.finding: At least three independent implementation families persist the same exploration artifacts and job boundaries.
market_evidence.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

operation.finding: The runtime optimizes low-latency query, interaction reduction, linked views, rendering, caching and cancellation.
operation.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

semantics.finding: Worksheet, chart, dashboard, selection, filter state and bookmark are first-class meanings distinct from report jobs and output artifacts.
semantics.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

user.finding: Analysts and information consumers iteratively explore; they are not report schedulers, filing publishers or distribution operators.
user.subject: interactive_analytics_exploration

name: Formal Reporting & Publication
sovereign_question: How can a report owner define, validate, execute, render, issue, distribute, correct and withdraw a durable analytical report whose inputs, parameters, renditions, recipients and evidence remain exact?

adoption.finding: Power BI Paginated Reports, Cognos Reporting, Oracle BI Publisher and JasperReports independently expose formal-reporting surfaces.
adoption.subject: formal_reporting_publication

authority.finding: Publication, issuance, disclosure and recipient selection are explicit authorities separate from source truth and notification transport.
authority.subject: formal_reporting_publication

economics.finding: Formal reporting engines and services are independently deployed, licensed, supported and capacity-managed.
economics.subject: formal_reporting_publication

interface.finding: Report definitions, parameters, scheduling APIs, output-format contracts and durable files form explicit adoption and exit surfaces.
interface.subject: formal_reporting_publication

job.finding: The owned job is to define, validate, execute, render, publish, distribute, correct and withdraw durable report artifacts.
job.subject: formal_reporting_publication

lifecycle.finding: Definition, job, run, output, publication, supersession, correction, recall and retention have independent state machines.
lifecycle.subject: formal_reporting_publication

market_evidence.finding: Four independent implementation families and reporting standards exhibit convergent lifecycle state.
market_evidence.subject: formal_reporting_publication

operation.finding: The runtime optimizes batch execution, pagination, multi-format rendering, bursting, scheduling, delivery, retention and replay.
operation.subject: formal_reporting_publication

semantics.finding: Report definition, template, parameter set, job, run, rendition, output artifact, schedule, delivery and job history are first-class state.
semantics.subject: formal_reporting_publication

user.finding: Report designers, publishers, schedulers, filing owners and recipients are distinguishable from interactive explorers.
user.subject: formal_reporting_publication
